title: Rapid Spanning Tree: The Complete Beginner's Guide

scenes.narration: Classic spanning tree can take fifty seconds to recover. That's a long time with no network. Rapid S T P does it in about six. Here's how.

lines.t: That's a long time with no network

scenes.heading: Fire doors that pop open
scenes.narration: Classic spanning tree is a fire marshal who waits twenty seconds before unlocking any door. Rapid S T P is a building where every floor manager talks to their neighbours constantly. If a door fails, a neighbour just agrees to open its own straight away. That quick chat is called proposal and agreement. Doors to end devices open instantly, because they're edge ports.

scenes.heading: Port states and roles
scenes.narration: The port states got simpler. Classic has four working states, and Rapid has just three. The roles also changed, because Rapid adds alternate and backup ports. Both are ready to take over the moment something fails.

scenes.heading: Common mix-ups
scenes.narration: Three mix-ups. Rapid S T P has three states, not five. An alternate port backs up the root port, while a backup port backs up a designated port. And on shared half duplex links, it falls back to slow timers.

items.wrong: Alternate backs up a designated port
items.right: Alternate backs up the root port

scenes.heading: Remember this
scenes.cta: Try the Courseiva Rapid STP lab
scenes.narration: So, to recap. Rapid S T P recovers in seconds, using handshakes instead of timers. It has three states and four roles. And Cisco's Rapid P V S T plus runs one copy per V L A N. Ready to practise? Try the Courseiva Rapid STP lab.

points.t: Rapid PVST+ runs one instance per VLAN
